learningObjective: Identify legal kernel launch configurations against A100 (sm_80) hardware limits.

canonicalClaims.claim: On A100 (sm_80): max threads per block = 1024; max blockDim = (1024, 1024, 64); max gridDim.x = 2^31 − 1; max gridDim.y = gridDim.z = 65535. Illegal launches return an error at `cudaGetLastError`.
nonImplications: Does not imply maximum legal launch is efficient.
Does not imply older compute capabilities share these limits.

misconceptions.claim: A single block can hold more than 1024 threads if no SMEM is used.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Threads-per-block cap is 1024 regardless of resource usage.

misconceptions.claim: nvcc silently truncates over-large blockDim to the nearest legal value.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The launch fails; no silent truncation.

misconceptions.claim: All grid dimensions are equal 65535 caps.
misconceptions.whyWrong: x is 2^31 − 1; y and z are 65535.

implementationFacts: Occupancy Calculator uses these limits + resource usage.
